# Appeal of Denial — Total Hip Replacement (CPT 27130)

**Governing Policy:** Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026
https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-313%20Hip%20Replace%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

**Re:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-09
**Member:** Emerson Alvarez
**Member ID:** W977514824
**Reference Number:** POC-4E415360FE-32022
**Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Missouri
**Procedure:** Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
**Surgeon:** Dr. Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Cigna Appeals Review Team,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a total hip replacement (CPT 27130). My claim was denied on 2026-08-09 with the stated reason that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this surgery is medically necessary, and I am asking Cigna to reconsider this decision based on the records already in my file.

## Why I believe the documentation supports my surgery

The denial notice does not specify which piece of documentation was considered incomplete. I want to lay out, in detail, what is already in my medical record so that Cigna's reviewers can see that the relevant clinical information has, in fact, been provided.

Cigna's own policy states that hip replacement is evaluated against specific criteria:

> "hip replacement is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met:"

Among the criteria the policy uses to evaluate the need for surgery is the requirement that conservative treatment be tried and fail, or be shown to be inappropriate:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

and

> "The medical record must clearly document why provider-directed non-surgical management is not appropriate."

and, in describing when hip replacement is appropriate more broadly:

> "• Conservative management or surgical fixation is not considered a reasonable option."

My records document the following conservative treatment, which I understand is the kind of information these criteria call for:

- **Symptom duration:** 24 months of progressive hip pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Physical therapy:** 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait, from 2026-03-03 to 2026-06-23, with 20 visits completed, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-15, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging:** A weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph on 2026-06-02 showing joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes.
- **Functional limitation:** I currently ambulate with a cane, am limited to walking one block, and cannot put on my shoes unassisted.
- **Exam findings:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- **No contraindications noted:** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

I want to note plainly that the specific published criteria for my underlying condition were not included in the materials I was given describing this policy, so I am not quoting the plan on that particular point. The excerpts above, describing the general requirement to document conservative treatment and its failure or inappropriateness, are the language I do have, and I believe my record — with specific dates, visit counts, and outcomes for physical therapy, medication, and injection — directly responds to that kind of documentation requirement.

If Cigna's reviewers believe a specific piece of documentation is still missing, I am asking that the denial letter or the appeal response identify exactly what that is, so my surgeon's office can supply it promptly.

## What I am asking for

I am requesting that Cigna reconsider this denial and approve the total hip replacement (CPT 27130) based on the clinical documentation described above, or, if something specific is still needed, tell me and my surgeon's office exactly what that is so it can be provided before the appeal deadline.

## Deadline and how I am submitting this appeal

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-05. I am submitting this appeal by logging into my.cigna.com to use the plan's appeal form, and/or by calling the number on my member card (1-800-244-6224), and by mailing this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial letter: [insert mailing address from denial letter].

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Emerson Alvarez
Member ID: W977514824
[Address]
[Phone number
